segments.narration: Thirty-two rats were found with their tails knotted together. That one is preserved, and it sits in a German museum.
It came out of a miller's fireplace at Buchheim in 1828, and it is still the largest example anybody has documented.
They called it a rat king. The name first meant a person who lived off everybody around him.
So how do thirty-two tails tie themselves? Rats pile up for warmth in winter, and sebum, sap and droppings freeze the tails together.
X-rays of a 1963 Dutch find show healed fractures. They lived like that for weeks. A living one turned up in Estonia in 2021.
